To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the general chi( (2)) test is the most suitable for detecting differences in the expression of weakly expressed genes; (ii) Audic and Clavrie's method is the most suitable when dealing with pairwise comparison of two samples, and (iii) a novel software, named IDEG6, has been developed and made available to the scientific community for the detection of differentially regulated genes.
the general chi( (2)) test is the best choice in multiple tag sampling, while Audic and Clavere's method is the best for pairwise comparisons.
the general chi( (2)) test is the most efficient method to use for detection of differentials expressed genes in a multiple tag sampling experiments.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new methodology for the detection of differentially regulated genes in multiple tag-sampling experiments, and its application to the analysis of data obtained from UniGene, a database of human expressed sequence tag (EST) sequences.
the development of statistical methodologies and software for detecting differentially expressed genes.
a comparative evaluation of statistical methods currently used in the analysis of gene expression data sets obtained from multiple tag sampling experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the choice of the statistical method to be used for the identification of differentially expressed tags in a multiple sampling experiment should be based on the specific experimental conditions and the nature of the biological question to be addressed.
, depending on the specific problem to be solved and the type of data to be analysed, the best statistical method to be used should be carefully chosen.
, for the detection of differentially regulated genes in multiple tag samples, the general chi2 test, as implemented in the IDEG6 package, represents the best choice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, when dealing with multiple tag sampling experiments in the case of weakly expressed genes, the use of the chi(2) statistical test is strongly recommended.
, in the analysis of multiple tag sampling experiments in which several biological replicates are available for each experimental condition, a general chi(2)-based test is the method of choice.
in multiple tag sampling the general chi( 2) test is the most appropriate for detecting differentially expressed genes, while for pairwise comparisons Audic and Clavie's method is the most efficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of the statistical method should be made according to the experimental design and the type of biological problem under study.
the choice of a method for detecting differentially expressed genes depends on the type of experimental design.

the general chi( 2) test is the most efficient method for the analysis of multiple tag sampling data, and it can be applied to detect differentially expressed genes also when the expression level of the gene under consideration is low.
